_meta.scope: Q-Day Index (published-spec scoring). NOT Q-Arena (circuits we run ourselves — separate artifact).
_meta.target_at_launch: RSA-2048 (single target). Bitcoin/ECDSA, Ethereum, TLS deferred to later chats.
_meta.sourcing_bar: vendor_published OR peer_reviewed ONLY. Press estimates and content-mill sources are barred.
schema_notes: Each numeric field carries paired provenance: <field>_source (URL), <field>_confidence (vendor_published | peer_reviewed), <field>_as_of (when the value was true / measured / published), and <field>_method (what kind of measurement the number is).

_method exists because 'two-qubit gate fidelity' is NOT one comparable quantity across vendors (XEB vs median ECR error vs randomized benchmarking vs direct RB vs analog/N-A). Do not rank the raw column without surfacing _method. This is the apples-to-oranges hazard the dashboard disclaimer must address.
null is an honest value. A null field with a caveat is correct and preferred over a fabricated or unverifiable number.

logical_qubits is 0 or null for essentially all standing hardware today — that is the honest point. Vendor 'logical qubit' claims are almost always QEC *demonstrations* (often via a partner virtualization layer), not always-on hardware capacity. Those go in notes, not in logical_qubits.
disclaimer_keys per system point at definitions written ONCE in docs/q-day-methodology.md (Chat C). Dashboard links the tag to that definition rather than duplicating prose.

glossary_terms (top level) is the deduplicated list of every technical term used in this file that needs a plain-language hover definition. Chat C writes the copy; Chat D's tooltip component reads from the single methodology source.
editorial_rules: Cite the paper, not the press release. Where a peer-reviewed or vendor-spec value differs from the rounded press number, the verified value wins and the gap is noted (press_vs_paper).
Cite the journal-of-record over the preprint where both exist and differ (readout_preprint_vs_published).
Neutrality firewall: present the number, never crown a winner. Reader concludes.

disclaimer_keys.analog_not_gate_model: System is an analog Hamiltonian simulator / field-programmable qubit array, not a gate-model machine. It has no two-qubit *gate* fidelity in the discrete-gate sense. An RSA-breaking (Shor) score is a gate-model question; a near-zero or N/A score here is a category difference, not a quality knock.
disclaimer_keys.press_vs_paper: The peer-reviewed or vendor-spec value differs from (usually is lower than) the rounded number in press coverage. This dataset cites the verified value.
disclaimer_keys.aq_not_qubit_count: IonQ's #AQ (Algorithmic Qubits) is an application-level benchmark score, NOT a count of physical or logical qubits. Forte's #AQ 36 colliding with its 36 physical qubits is a coincidence that invites misreading.
disclaimer_keys.logical_qubits_are_demos: Reported 'logical qubits' for this system come from a quantum-error-correction demonstration (often with a partner virtualization layer), not a standing always-on hardware property.
disclaimer_keys.milestone_not_cloud: Published as a scale / yield / advantage milestone, not as a generally-available cloud machine at announcement. Full per-device calibration may never have been released.
disclaimer_keys.readout_preprint_vs_published: A spec value differs between the arXiv preprint and the published journal version. This dataset cites the published journal-of-record value.
disclaimer_keys.calibration_snapshot_drifts: Vendor publishes this metric as live calibration data that drifts daily, OR as a dated median in a paper. The value here is a fixed dated snapshot (_as_of), not a current live readout, and will not match a calibration page pulled on a different day.
disclaimer_keys.modality_not_comparable: Cross-modality comparison caveat: qubit counts and fidelities across superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom and photonic systems are not directly comparable (e.g. all-to-all trapped-ion connectivity vs fixed superconducting lattice; 56 trapped-ion qubits are not '100 fewer' than 156 superconducting qubits in any simple sense).
disclaimer_keys.historical_anchor: Included primarily as a prior-generation time-series point for the (internal, held-back) trajectory model — not presented as a current frontier machine.

target.name: RSA-2048
target.anchor_citation: Gidney 2025, 'How to factor 2048-bit RSA integers with less than a million noisy qubits'
target.notes: Single launch target. The active anchor is the 2025 Gidney estimate (<1M qubits, <1 week); the 2019 Gidney & Ekera estimate (~20M qubits, ~8 hours) is retained as the prior anchor for the 'moving target' caveat — the ~20x fall happened on algorithmic and error-correction progress alone, hardware assumptions held identical. The scoring formula allows swapping this anchor for a different target (Bitcoin/ECDSA etc.) later without hard-coding RSA assumptions.
target.anchor_prior_citation: Gidney & Ekera 2019, 'How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits'

systems.release_year_notes: IBM docs date Heron r2 to July 2024. The widely-cited Nov 2024 date is the Quantum Developer Conference announcement, not first release. Heron r3 (July 2025) and Nighthawk r1 (Dec 2025) are later and out of scope for this entry.
systems.logical_qubits_notes: No standing logical qubits. IBM's error-correction work (e.g. qLDPC roadmap) is forward-looking, not always-on capacity on this device.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: WEAKEST-SOURCED FIDELITY IN THE SET — flagged deliberately. IBM does not publish a single fixed per-device 2Q gate fidelity; it publishes live calibration data (drifts daily) and dated medians in papers. Value shown is derived from a dated peer-reviewed median ECR error snapshot (7.57e-3 -> ~0.99243 fidelity) as of 2024-08-01. This is IBM's CZ/ECR two-qubit metric, NOT directly comparable to Google's XEB or trapped-ion RB. Treat as a dated snapshot, not a current value.
systems.single_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Derived from median SX error 2.41e-4 as of 2024-08-01.
systems.error_correction_below_threshold_notes: Not demonstrated below-threshold surface-code scaling on this device in the Willow sense.
systems.notes: IBM does not publish a single fixed two-qubit gate fidelity; it reports live calibration data that drifts daily, alongside dated medians in publications. The value shown is a dated peer-reviewed median, chosen so the figure is reproducible. Heron r2 can execute roughly 5,000 two-qubit gate operations in a circuit — a measure of circuit depth, not gate fidelity.

systems.logical_qubits_notes: Distance-7 surface code: a single logical qubit from 101 physical qubits, 0.143% error per cycle, beyond breakeven (2.4x its best physical qubit lifetime). This is a demonstration of one below-threshold logical qubit, not a multi-logical-qubit standing register. Recorded as 1 with this explicit caveat rather than 0, because the below-threshold demonstration is the load-bearing signal for the formula.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Google does NOT headline an isolated 2Q RB fidelity. It leads with logical error-per-cycle (0.143% d=7) and random-circuit-sampling XEB. The load-bearing signal for this system is error_correction_below_threshold = true, not a single 2Q gate number. Left null rather than back-converting an XEB figure into a misleadingly comparable 'fidelity'.
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: Nature paper: mean T1 = 68 us (+/- 13). NOTE press_vs_paper: Google's own blog says 'approaching 100 us'; we cite the peer-reviewed 68 us, not the marketing figure.
systems.cloud_available_notes: Research device; not a general-access cloud machine at publication.
systems.error_correction_below_threshold_notes: First clear below-threshold demonstration: logical error suppressed by Lambda = 2.14 +/- 0.02 per +2 code distance, d=3 -> d=5 -> d=7. Strongest such published evidence of any system in this set. Load-bearing for the scoring formula.
systems.notes: Google's blog describes coherence as approaching 100 microseconds, while the peer-reviewed paper reports a mean T1 of 68 microseconds; the published figure is shown here. Willow's defining result is its demonstrated below-threshold error correction, not any single gate-fidelity number.

systems.release_year_notes: 56-qubit upgrade announced June 2024 (H2-1 upgraded from 32 to 56 qubits).
systems.logical_qubits_notes: The widely-cited '4 logical qubits, 800x error reduction' is a Microsoft/Quantinuum QEC demonstration using Azure's qubit-virtualization layer, not a standing always-on property of the hardware. Recorded as 0 standing; demo noted here.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Paper value 99.843(5)%. NOTE press_vs_paper: Quantinuum's own press release rounds to '99.9% / three nines'; we cite the peer-reviewed 99.843%.
systems.single_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Quantinuum reports single-qubit fidelity >99.99% in materials; left null pending a paired peer-reviewed/spec-sheet value with a clean method tag rather than a rounded press figure.
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: Quantinuum's H2 data sheet does not list per-system T1/T2 in microseconds. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ hyperfine qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second-to-minute scale — orders of magnitude longer than the microsecond-scale T1/T2 reported by superconducting systems — but this is a property of the ion physics, not a system-specific calibration figure that meets our sourcing bar. Left null in the microsecond column to preserve cross-system comparability.
systems.error_correction_below_threshold_notes: QEC demonstrations exist (with partners) but below-threshold surface-code scaling in the Willow sense is not the claim here.
systems.notes: With all-to-all connectivity from trapped-ion shuttling, a 56-qubit H2-1 is not meaningfully "100 qubits behind" a 156-qubit superconducting machine — connectivity and gate fidelity trade against raw qubit count. Comparing qubit counts across these architectures is misleading.
systems.t2_coherence_us_notes: Quantinuum's H2 data sheet does not list per-system T1/T2 in microseconds. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ hyperfine qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second-to-minute scale — orders of magnitude longer than the microsecond-scale T1/T2 reported by superconducting systems — but this is a property of the ion physics, not a system-specific calibration figure that meets our sourcing bar. Left null in the microsecond column to preserve cross-system comparability.

systems.physical_qubits_notes: 36 physical Yb-171 ion qubits. DO NOT confuse with #AQ 36 (Algorithmic Qubits) — a coincidentally-equal application benchmark SCORE, not a qubit count. See aq_not_qubit_count.
systems.logical_qubits_notes: IonQ logical qubits are roadmap, not present on Forte.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Vendor page: 2Q gate error ~0.4% -> ~99.6% fidelity, measured by Direct Randomized Benchmarking. Corroborated by peer-reviewed benchmarking of Forte at 30q/#AQ29 (arXiv:2308.05071, DRB across 435 gate pairs).
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: IonQ's Forte page describes what T1 and T2 mean but does not publish numerical values for the system. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second scale — orders of magnitude longer than superconducting microsecond-scale times — but no Forte-specific number meets our sourcing bar (vendor data sheet or peer-reviewed paper). Vendor does separately publish a SPAM error of ~0.5%.
systems.notes: IonQ's "#AQ 36" is an application-level benchmark score, not a count of qubits; that it happens to equal Forte's 36 physical qubits is a coincidence. The two are unrelated quantities and should not be conflated.
systems.t2_coherence_us_notes: IonQ's Forte page describes what T1 and T2 mean but does not publish numerical values for the system. Trapped-ion 171Yb+ qubits have intrinsic coherence on the second scale — orders of magnitude longer than superconducting microsecond-scale times — but no Forte-specific number meets our sourcing bar (vendor data sheet or peer-reviewed paper). Vendor does separately publish a SPAM error of ~0.5%.

systems.topology: 20 flux-tunable transmon qubits, square lattice with tunable couplers
systems.release_year_notes: General availability on AWS Braket announced May 2024; the underlying device is described in arXiv 2408.12433.
systems.logical_qubits_notes: No standing logical qubits demonstrated on Garnet. IQM's roadmap targets 150-qubit scaling rather than near-term error correction on this device.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Median two-qubit CZ gate fidelity 99.51%, measured across 30 qubit pairs. Maximum on a single pair reaches 99.8%. This is IQM's native two-qubit gate; not directly comparable to Google's XEB, IBM's median ECR, or trapped-ion randomized benchmarking.
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: The 2408.12433 paper characterizes the 20-qubit Garnet device but does not headline a single median T1 figure in microseconds for the deployed system. A separate 2024 IQM milestone reported T1 ~0.96 ms on a planar transmon test device, but that is a fabrication-quality milestone, not the 20-qubit Garnet's operating spec. Left null rather than mix the two.
systems.cloud_available_notes: Available on AWS Braket (EU Stockholm region), May 2024 onwards.
systems.error_correction_below_threshold_notes: Below-threshold surface-code scaling has not been demonstrated on Garnet.
systems.notes: Europe's most-deployed superconducting platform, with a peer-reviewed paper publishing every required spec. IQM separately reported a 99.91% two-qubit gate fidelity milestone on a test device in mid-2024 — that figure is for fabrication-quality demonstration, not the operating spec of the 20-qubit Garnet, and is not used here. A larger 54-qubit Emerald QPU is also available on Braket as of 2025; out of scope for this Garnet entry.

systems.release_year_notes: Launched Nov 2022 as the first publicly accessible neutral-atom quantum computer.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Aquila is an ANALOG Hamiltonian simulator (FPQA), not a gate-model machine. It has no discrete two-qubit gate fidelity. Null is the correct, honest value here — NOT a missing number. See analog_not_gate_model.
systems.notes: The largest raw qubit count in the set at 256, but Aquila is an analog Hamiltonian simulator, not a gate-model machine — it has no two-qubit gate fidelity and no gate-model pathway to factoring RSA. It is marked N/A rather than given a low score: a category difference, not a quality judgment.

systems.topology: reconfigurable neutral-atom array (Rydberg), analog Hamiltonian evolution
systems.release_year_notes: Orion Alpha is Pasqal's first-generation production QPU; Orion Beta ("Ruby") was installed at Genci (France) and Forschungszentrum Juelich during 2024-2025.
systems.physical_qubits_notes: 100 atoms in analog mode per Pasqal's Orion Beta technical overview (Orion Alpha and Beta share the 100-qubit specification). Pasqal has experimentally trapped over 1,100 atoms in larger arrays separately.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Orion Alpha operates in analog mode (Hamiltonian evolution via Rydberg interactions), not as a gate-model machine. It has no discrete two-qubit gate fidelity in the standard sense. Pasqal's roadmap targets gate-based digital operation in future generations (Orion Gamma onwards).
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: Pasqal reports coherence on the tens-of-milliseconds scale for neutral-atom Rydberg qubits, but does not publish a per-system T1/T2 spec in microseconds.
systems.cloud_available_notes: Available via Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Marketplace, and Pasqal's own user portal.
systems.notes: Pasqal's first-generation production neutral-atom QPU, deployed in HPC centers (Genci in France, Forschungszentrum Juelich in Germany). Like QuEra Aquila, it operates as an analog Hamiltonian simulator rather than a gate-model machine — marked N/A as a category difference, not a quality judgment. Pasqal's roadmap (Orion Gamma 2026, Vela, Pegasus, Centaurus through 2030) targets gate-based digital operation with eventual logical qubits.

systems.release_year_notes: Announced Oct 2023 as next-gen system 'planned for release next year' — a preview/in-development milestone, not a generally-available cloud machine at announcement. See milestone_not_cloud.
systems.physical_qubits_notes: 1,180 atoms loaded in a 1,225-site array. First system to cross 1,000 physical qubits. Sourcing note: the announcement was carried widely in press; the underlying qubit-count and readout claims trace to Atom Computing and to the peer-reviewed PRX Quantum readout paper (Yb-171 nuclear spin). Press-only restatements do not themselves clear the bar.
systems.logical_qubits_notes: Microsoft/Atom '24 entangled / 28 corrected logical qubits' (Nov 2024) is a QEC demonstration via Azure's virtualization layer, not standing hardware capacity. Recorded as 0 standing; demo noted.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: 99.6% reported via Microsoft (integration partner, vendor_published). This is a LATER (Nov 2024) milestone, not the spec of the Oct 2023 announcement system — _as_of reflects that. Method tag is generic ('vendor_reported') because the partner blog does not state the benchmarking protocol; flagged low-confidence-on-method accordingly.
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: Neutral-atom 171Yb nuclear-spin qubits have demonstrated coherence on the tens-of-seconds scale in vendor materials (the widely-cited 40-second figure) — far longer than superconducting microsecond-scale T1/T2 — but this is reported as a qubit-memory record, not as the system-level T1/T2 specification used here. Left null in the microsecond column rather than force a non-comparable figure into it.
systems.cloud_available_notes: The 1,180-qubit next-gen system was in development at announcement; not a general cloud machine then. Marked false with caveat rather than asserting access we cannot source.
systems.notes: The highest physical qubit count of any scored system. The qubit count comes from a 2023 announcement and the gate fidelity from a 2024 partner publication — different dates and sources, shown with their respective dates rather than blended into a single figure.
systems.t2_coherence_us_notes: Neutral-atom 171Yb nuclear-spin qubits have demonstrated coherence on the tens-of-seconds scale in vendor materials (the widely-cited 40-second figure) — far longer than superconducting microsecond-scale T1/T2 — but this is reported as a qubit-memory record, not as the system-level T1/T2 specification used here. Left null in the microsecond column rather than force a non-comparable figure into it.

systems.release_year_notes: Public launch Dec 23, 2024. (Plan listed 'Ankaa ~84q'; current system is Ankaa-3.)
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: Rigetti reports TWO 2Q fidelities: 99.0% median iSWAP (universal gate) and 99.5% median fSim (specialized, for RCS). Headline value here is the 99.0% iSWAP because iSWAP is the general-purpose universal gate relevant to a Shor-type circuit; the 99.5% fSim is noted but not used as the headline to avoid overstating general-purpose fidelity.

two_qubit_gate_fidelity_alt.notes: Specialized fSim gate, useful for random circuit sampling; not the general-purpose universal gate.

systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: Rigetti cites improved T1 baseline (SQMS/Fermilab metal-deposition work) qualitatively; no paired peer-reviewed/spec numeric us value sourced to the bar. Null rather than estimate.
systems.cloud_available_notes: Available on Rigetti QCS at launch; Braket + Azure stated as coming Q1 2025.
systems.notes: Specifications are vendor-published (an investor press release); no peer-reviewed paper was available for these figures. Rigetti reports two distinct two-qubit fidelities — 99.0% for the general-purpose iSWAP gate and 99.5% for the specialized fSim gate. The general-purpose figure is used here.

systems.release_year_notes: Published in Physical Review Letters 134, 090601 (3 March 2025); preprint arXiv:2412.11924 (Dec 2024).
systems.logical_qubits_notes: A later device, Zuchongzhi 3.2 (107q, Dec 2025), is reported to demonstrate below-threshold QEC — out of scope for this 3.0 entry but a future trajectory/scored candidate.
systems.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: 99.62% two-qubit (simultaneous) gate fidelity per published PRL.
systems.readout_fidelity_notes: Published PRL value 99.13%. NOTE readout_preprint_vs_published: the arXiv preprint states 99.18%; we cite the published journal-of-record 99.13%.
systems.t1_coherence_us_notes: 72 us reported as average coherence time. Reported as a single coherence figure in the paper; placed in T1 with this caveat rather than split into separate T1/T2.
systems.t2_coherence_us_notes: Paper reports an average coherence (72 us) rather than separately-stated T1 and T2. Not duplicated into T2.
systems.cloud_available_notes: 3.0-series reported as opened for commercial use via China Telecom's Tianyan cloud platform (Oct 2025). Access may be region-constrained; flag if a conservative stance is preferred. Set true on the basis of the cloud availability report; revisit in Chat D if region-gating warrants a separate field.
systems.error_correction_below_threshold_notes: 3.0 itself is an advantage/RCS demonstration, not below-threshold QEC. (3.2 successor reportedly is — future entry.)
systems.notes: The best-sourced entry in the set: a peer-reviewed Physical Review Letters paper reporting every required figure. Its readout fidelity differs between the preprint (99.18%) and the published version (99.13%); the published journal value is shown.

historical_anchors.physical_qubits_notes: 54-qubit chip, 53 active in the supremacy experiment.
historical_anchors.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: ~0.6% average 2Q error -> ~99.4%, via XEB. Confirm exact figure against paper body before any public use.
historical_anchors.notes: Google trajectory anchor (Sycamore 2019 -> Willow 2024). Not a current frontier machine.

historical_anchors.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: IBM layer-fidelity paper (arXiv:2311.05933) characterizes a 127q Eagle (ibm_sherbrooke) via layer fidelity / EPLG, not a single comparable 2Q number. Left null for the anchor; the qubit-count + year is what the trajectory needs.
historical_anchors.notes: IBM trajectory anchor (Eagle 2021 -> Heron r1 2023 -> Heron r2 2024). Powered the 2,880 two-qubit-gate 2023 utility experiment.

historical_anchors.two_qubit_gate_fidelity_notes: IBM published Condor as a scale/yield milestone and did not release full per-device calibration as for cloud devices. Honest nulls across fidelity/coherence.
historical_anchors.notes: Highest raw qubit count IBM has published, but a milestone with mostly null performance fields by design — the clearest case of 'null is the honest value'.

announced_not_scored.reason: Roadmap / fusion-based architecture targeting ~1M physical qubits; no peer-reviewed or vendor-published specs for our required fields (per-device 2Q gate fidelity, T1/T2 in our sense) on a deployed machine. Does not clear the §4 bar.
announced_not_scored.notes: Footnote only. Revisit if qualifying specs are published.

announced_not_scored.reason: Photonic (CV / GBS) architecture. Published work (e.g. Borealis GBS in Nature) is real but does not map onto the gate-model 2Q-fidelity / T1-T2 schema this index scores. No qualifying values for our required fields.
announced_not_scored.notes: Footnote only. Photonic CV systems are a structural mismatch for the launch schema, similar in spirit to the analog caveat.

announced_not_scored.reason: Boson 4, available on Google Cloud Marketplace, is a single cat-qubit chip (not a multi-qubit processor) — it demonstrates a >7-minute bit-flip suppression record but does not have the physical_qubits + two_qubit_gate_fidelity combination this schema scores. Multi-qubit follow-ons (Helium 16-qubit, Lithium) are on the roadmap, not deployed.
announced_not_scored.notes: Important architectural alternative — cat qubits target hardware-level bit-flip protection so error correction only needs to handle phase flips. Worth revisiting when Helium or later deploys with published multi-qubit specs.

announced_not_scored.reason: Diraq has a peer-reviewed Nature paper demonstrating >99% two-qubit CZ gate fidelity on industrially-fabricated silicon quantum-dot devices (collaboration with imec, 300mm CMOS) — peer-reviewed credentials, but the demonstrations are on two-qubit double-quantum-dot devices, not a deployed N-qubit processor.
announced_not_scored.notes: Silicon spin qubits offer a manufacturing-scalability story unique among the candidates. Worth revisiting when a multi-qubit Diraq processor with published system-level specs ships.

outreach_candidates.reason: Photonic fusion-based architecture; targeting ~1M physical qubits. No qualifying per-device specs yet.
Photonic continuous-variable / Gaussian Boson Sampling; structural schema mismatch.
Single cat-qubit Boson 4 deployed; multi-qubit follow-on Helium on roadmap.
Peer-reviewed silicon spin qubit fidelity; no deployed multi-qubit processor yet.
